facts.text: Christianshavn was founded in the early 17th century by King Christian IV as an extension of Copenhagen's fortifications.
The area was originally laid out as an independent merchant town inspired by Dutch cities before being incorporated into Copenhagen.
Christianshavn’s canals give it the most nautical atmosphere in Copenhagen, with tree‑lined waterways packed with boats and colorful houses.
The freetown Christiania, a self‑governing community, emerged in 1971 from abandoned military barracks and now sits within Christianshavn.
The former headquarters of Nordea now serves as Hotel NH Collection Copenhagen along the harbourfront, a notable repurposing of historic banking buildings.
Christianshavn metro station, located at Christianshavns Torv, connects the neighborhood to the rest of the city via the Copenhagen Metro.
